test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 6 Sept 2022 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: When silver nitrate solution is added to sodium chloride solution:

options.text: silver will deposit on the surface of the reaction vessel
a white precipitate of silver chloride is formed
a white precipitate of sodium nitrate is obtained

solution:
The correct answer is __**a white precipitate of silver chloride is formed**__ .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Silver nitrate**

 
 
• Silver Nitrate is used as the marker during Election.
 
• When silver nitrate is exposed to sunlight, it breaks down to give black/brown silver oxides and nitric acid i.e.,
 
 
• AgNO3 + H2O → AgO + HNO3 (aq)
 
 
 
• Silver nitrate decomposes when exposed to the sunlight, so to prevent it from decomposition, silver nitrate is placed in brown colour bottles as brown bottle cuts the passage of light through it.
 
 
 
• **Sodium chloride**
 
 
• Sodium Chloride is also known as Salt.
 
 
• It is an ionic compound with the chemical formula NaCl.
 
• It has a ratio of 1:1 of sodium and chloride ions, With molar masses of 22.99 and 35.45 g/mol respectively.
 
• 100 g of NaCl contains 39.34 g Na and 60.66 g Cl.
 
• Sodium chloride is used in the Solvay process to produce sodium carbonate and calcium chloride.
 
• In the Mannheim process and in the Hargreaves process, sodium chloride is used for the production of sodium sulfate and hydrochloric acid.
